title: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)

sections.label: Scam cases versus Police investigators
sections.summary: The Minister said scam cases rose 400% over five years while Police investigators increased only 7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In his characteristic direct manner, the hon Minister shared some stark facts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He said over the past five years, scam cases went up 400%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The number of Police investigators, on the other hand, increased only by 7%.

sections.label: Value of SPF investigated cases
sections.summary: A Parliamentary Question response showed the subject matter value of SPF-investigated cases from 2017 to 2021 was $4.49 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: From a response to a Parliamentary Question I filed, I noted that between 2017 and 2021 the subject matter value of cases investigated by the Singapore Police Force (SPF) was $4.49 billion.

sections.label: Police manpower shortage and morale
sections.summary: The Minister admitted the Police Force faces a severe manpower shortage that would ultimately impact morale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Earlier this month on 6 February 2024, the hon Minister in response to a question posed by the hon Leader of Opposition in this House, candidly admitted that whilst Police officers have strong esprit de corp, the Police Force is facing a severe manpower shortage and this would ultimately have an impact on morale.

sections.label: Home Team Science and Technology Agency
sections.summary: Much of the innovation was driven by the Home Team Science and Technology Agency, set up in end 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Much of the innovation was driven by the Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) which was set up in end 2019.

sections.label: Volunteer recruitment and MHA statement
sections.summary: Recruitment figures for Citizen on Patrol volunteers and Voluntary Special Constabulary officers appear generally downtrending; MHA said Mr Chan showed susceptibility to foreign actors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this regard, I have sought and reviewed the figures that the Ministry provided to me on the recruitment numbers of Citizen on Patrol volunteers as well as Voluntary Special Constabulary officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It seems to me that the recruitment figures are on the downtrend, generally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I also look forward to hearing the plans that the Home Team has to strengthen its partnership with these volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MHA said that Mr Chan had shown susceptibility to be influenced by foreign actors and willingness to advance their interests.

sections.label: Marriage and right of entry
sections.summary: The Minister of State said marriage to a Singaporean did not grant automatic entry or long-term stay approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister of State also said that marriage to a Singaporean did not grant automatic right of entry into Singapore or approval for a long-term stay.

sections.label: PMLA completion and foreign spouses
sections.summary: Of 7,200 annual ICA applications, only around 3,000 applicants completed the PMLA, and Singaporeans marrying foreigners need clarity on their spouse's stay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Of the 7,200 applications ICA process annually, only around 3,000 applicants completed the PMLA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singaporeans intending to marry a foreigner must have a clearer picture on whether their spouse will be able to remain with them in Singapore, ideally before they get married.

sections.label: Increase in regular officers
sections.summary: The number of regular officers rose from about 8,800 in 2013 to more than 10,000 today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A brief comparison of the number of officers from 2013 to date shows an increase from about 8,800 regulars to more than 10,000 today.

sections.label: Auxiliary police officer nationalities
sections.summary: 68% of APOs are Singaporeans while 32% are Malaysians and Taiwanese, and the Minister affirmed the need to recruit foreign APOs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Sixty-eight percent of APOs are Singaporeans, while the balance 32% are Malaysians and Taiwanese.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In answer to a Parliamentary Question (PQ) I filed in January, the Minister affirmed the need to allow auxiliary police forces to recruit foreign APOs to meet the increasing demand for security services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was further mentioned that besides Taiwan, some other source countries for APOs being considered are China, India, the Philippines and Myanmar.

sections.label: SME security agencies digital adoption
sections.summary: In 2019, 98% of SME security agencies adopted a stage one digital solution and 82% a stage two solution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ministry reported then that in 2019, 98% of SME security agencies had adopted at least one stage one digital solution, while 82% had adopted at least one stage two solution as recommended by the security industry digital plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As one of the biggest bugbears of security officers are the long 12-hour shifts, it will be useful to know whether the adoption of these technologies has resulted in shorter working shifts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is the Ministry's assessment, would be entailed to move to an eight-hour shift?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With the further concerted efforts to improve the image and working conditions of security officers, does the Ministry also detect any change in the demographic profile of those in the industry?

sections.label: Security Industry Transformation Map
sections.summary: The Security Industry Transformation Map was launched in 2018 and refreshed in November 2022 for integrated facilities management.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Consequently, the Security Industry Transformation Map was launched in 2018, to uplift the private security industry to meet these evolving security challenges.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In November 2022, Ministry announced a refreshed version, to prepare the industry in delivering security services as part of integrated facilities management.

sections.label: Recidivism and scam cases
sections.summary: A 14 February 2024 report showed higher two-year recidivism for the 2021 release cohort, and 2023 scam cases rose 46.8% with $651.8 million lost.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A report released on 14 February 2024 by Singapore Prison Service indicated an increase in the two-year recidivism rate for the 2021 release cohort, primarily due to higher recidivism among repeat drug offenders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2023, scam cases in Singapore surged by 46.8% compared to 2022, with victims losing a total of $651.8 million.

sections.label: SPF IO workload and turnover
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for insight into SPF investigation officers' workload and average turnover from first information reports to AGC recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister provide some insight into the workload of our SPF IOs as well as the average turnover of investigations from first information reports (FIRs) to making recommendations to the AGC?

sections.label: Home Team Transformation plans
sections.summary: The passage asks what plans exist for Home Team Transformation amid a tight labour market, covering operational capabilities, training, manpower reliance and technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: At the same time, the Home Team is also confronted with a tight labour market and a slowing workforce growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I wish to ask what are the plans moving forward for the Home Team's Transformation to meet these exacting challenges – especially in the areas of operational capabilities, training reality and preparedness, reduction of its reliance on manpower and helping our Home Team officers to focus on key operational tasks and eradicate tasks which can be done with technology and process improvements?

sections.label: Proposed law status and implementation
sections.summary: The passage asks for updates on a proposed law, whether it will be implemented, and how it balances social order with freedom of expression.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide updates on the status of this proposed law?

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will it in fact be implemented and if so, how will this new law seek to balance the maintenance of social order with the need for freedom of expression in our society?

sections.label: Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act update
sections.summary: The passage asks MHA for an update on the planned Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act, which the Prime Minister mentioned in his 2021 National Day Rally speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In any event, in 2021, the Prime Minister – in his National Day Rally speech – addressed the topic of racial harmony and indicated that there was a plan to introduce a Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I will be grateful if MHA can provide an update on this?

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Hamas' attack on Israeli civilians on 7 October was shocking and Singapore had called it an act of terror.

sections.label: Police and NParks protest prohibition
sections.summary: The passage states that in Singapore the Police and NParks have prohibited protests and demonstrations on this matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In Singapore, the Police and NParks have – in my view – rightly prohibited protests and demonstrations on this matter.

sections.label: Openness and misinformation vulnerability
sections.summary: The passage states that openness renders Singapore vulnerable to misinformation, manipulation and divisive narratives, including false foreign donation campaigns posing as humanitarian campaigns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While this openness is a strength, it also renders us vulnerable to misinformation, manipulation and divisive narratives propagated through various channels, including social media and online platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There are also false foreign donation campaigns in the guise of humanitarian campaigns that may take advantage of the generosity of Singaporeans.

sections.label: National security and foreign influence
sections.summary: Asks about Singapore's national security outlook and how MHA will preserve security, cohesion and racial harmony while giving Singaporeans a safe platform for humanitarian efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In light of the increased risk of foreign influence and the global uncertainty, what is the outlook of national security in Singapore; and what are the ways in which MHA will or have undertaken to ensure that our national security, social cohesion and racial harmony are preserved while – at the same time – allowing for well-intentioned Singaporeans who resonate with increasing humanitarian causes around the world to have a safe platform in Singapore to channel their efforts and resources towards constructive narratives and initiatives?

sections.label: Online pro-drug messages
sections.summary: Online platforms and Telegram channels spread pro-drug messages and normalise substance abuse, challenging Singapore's efforts to stay drug-free.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The rise of online platforms and social networks groups on Telegram channels for instance, has facilitated the dissemination of pro-drug messages and normalisation of substance abuse – posing a significant challenge to Singapore's efforts to maintain a drug-free society.

sections.label: MHA, community partners, YRSG
sections.summary: Asks how MHA, community partners and YRSG work to improve outcomes for desistors and prevent rising drug abuse in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What are the ways that MHA have undertaken together with community partners and YRSG to ensure better outcomes for desistors and keep our guard up to prevent the increase in drug abuse in Singapore and fellow Singaporeans?

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore is swimming against the tide in its fight against drugs.

sections.label: Five 14-year-olds arrested
sections.summary: Among those arrested last year were five 14-year-olds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Among those arrested last year were five 14-year-olds.

sections.label: IMH survey average starting age
sections.summary: A 2023 Institute of Mental Health survey found drug users in Singapore start taking illegal substances at an average age of around 16.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An Institute of Mental Health (IMH) survey in 2023 shared that the average age when drug users in Singapore start taking illegal substances is around 16.

sections.label: Scam cases and losses
sections.summary: On 18 February 2024, The Straits Times reported 46,563 cases in 2023 where victims lost $651 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 18 February 2024, The Straits Times reported there were 46,563 cases in 2023 where victims lost $651 million.

sections.label: New drug abusers and youth prevention
sections.summary: CNB reported new drug abusers arrested rose 18% last year, over half under 30, and asks about the 2023 Inter-Ministry Committee's plans, timeline and vaporiser coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Worryingly, CNB reported new drug abusers arrested have increased 18% last year and even more concerning is that more than half of new drug abusers are aged well below 30, with the youngest being 14.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Notably, the digital space continues to be an avenue for the spread of misinformation and aid transactions to occur swiftly and anonymously, which makes drug detection challenging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I appreciate that an Inter-Ministry Committee on Drug Prevention for Youths was formed in 2023 to set targeted strategies with an ecosystem approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can MHA also share in greater detail plans by the Inter-Ministry Committee, the implementation timeline and if they will also address vaporiser use, in addition to drugs and NPS?

sections.label: Update and second chances review
sections.summary: MHA is asked for an update on progress and whether laws like the Registration of Criminals Act can be reviewed to offer second chances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Can MHA provide an update on what we have done and how far have we come thus far and whether laws, such as the Registration of Criminals Act, can be reviewed to offer them second chances?

sections.label: Recreational cannabis abuse statistics
sections.summary: Cannabis ranks second most commonly abused drug for new abusers, with a 17% increase between 2022 and 2023, and almost two-thirds of new abusers are below 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The statistics in Singapore for abusers of recreational cannabis are highly concerning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It ranks as the second most commonly abused drug for new abusers, with a 17% increase between 2022 and 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What is even more concerning is that almost two-thirds of the new abusers are below 30 years of age.

sections.label: Cannabis share of drug use disorder
sections.summary: Approximately 41% of all drug use disorder cases are due to cannabis abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Of all drug use disorder cases, approximately 41% is due to cannabis abuse.

sections.label: Enforcement and rehabilitation double-pronged approach
sections.summary: With rising drug abusers, enforcement and monitoring must be matched by rehabilitation support, since 51% of new abusers arrested in 2023 were under 30 and repeat offenders form the bulk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With the constant increase in drug abusers in Singapore, but repeat and new offenders, it is critical that our enforcement and monitoring of drug usage is matched by rehabilitation support in a double-pronged approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is especially so since 51% of new abusers arrested in 2023 were under 30, but also because repeat offenders still form the bulk of drug abusers.

sections.label: ASEAN cooperation against junta allies
sections.summary: UK and China have taken sanctions and arrest warrants, so ASEAN should consider cooperating against allies of the Myanmar junta involved in scam farms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: UK has also placed sanctions to prevent British citizens and companies from any dealings with designated people and entities and sanctioned actors in Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is also reflected in China, where it has issued arrest warrants for major players – especially those who work and interact with the Myanmar junta.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In that light, we should consider how ASEAN can cooperate in dealing with the allies of the junta regime who are actively involved or – quite possibly – overseeing scam farms.

sections.label: Scam prevention and public education
sections.summary: The passage asks what MHA is doing to prevent scams and help citizens identify them, citing 2022 and 2023 scam figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, we need to also educate the public and each individual on all the potential avenues for scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, I ask in conclusion, what is MHA doing to strengthen our ability to prevent scams and to help our citizens identify scams?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The headline numbers for 2022 were 33,669 scams and cybercrime cases and $660.7 million lost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In the recently released statistics by the Police for 2023, the total amount of loss deceased slightly by 1.3% to $651.8 million but the number of scam cases increased significantly by 49.6% to 50,376.

sections.label: Scam losses and case increase
sections.summary: Scam losses stayed flat at $650 million last year, but cases rose 46% to 46,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Thanks to such efforts, scam losses stayed flat at $650 million last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, the amount remains significant and of worry is the steep increase of cases by 46% to 46,000.

sections.label: Rising scam cases in Singapore
sections.summary: The number of cases in Singapore continues to increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, the number of cases in Singapore continues to increase.

sections.label: Online Criminal Harms Act impact
sections.summary: The passage asks how much impact the Ministry expects the Online Criminal Harms Act to have on reducing online criminal activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How much impact does the Ministry expect the Online Criminal Harms Act (OCHA) to have on reducing such online criminal activities?

sections.label: Investments in anti-scam capabilities
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will draw public and private investments into developing anti-scam capabilities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry look into drawing public and private investments into developing anti-scam capabilities in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These capabilities have the potential to be developed into a leading industry's products and services, like the role anti-virus software play in digital devices.

sections.label: Scams as main crime driver
sections.summary: Scams were the main driver of crime in 2023, with over 46,000 cases and more than SGD$650 million lost.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: However, similar to 2022, scams were the main driver of crime in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There were more than 46,000 reported scam cases, which is a nearly 50% increase from 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And the total amount lost to scams was more than SGD$650 million.

sections.label: New drug abusers arrested increase
sections.summary: Singapore's drug situation is generally under control, but new drug abuser arrests rose 18% in 2023, over half under age 30.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Our drug situation remains generally under control, but in 2023 there was an 18% increase in the number of new drug abusers arrested in Singapore, and more than half of them were under the age of 30.

sections.label: Cannabis abuser arrests high
sections.summary: Cannabis abuser arrests in Singapore reached a 10-year high in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Cannabis abuser arrests in Singapore were at a 10-year high last year, in 2023.

sections.label: Cannabis harm and legalisation effects
sections.summary: Claims that cannabis is harmless are untrue; studies show cannabis causes brain damage and psychiatric illness, and legalisation linked to more disorders, suicides and hospitalisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: These are all untruths, blatant untruths, much like what tobacco companies used to claim that smoking tobacco, smoking cigarettes was harmless.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But the scientific evidence is that cannabis abuse causes harm to the abuser's health.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Studies show quite clearly that cannabis can cause irreversible brain damage, brain shrinkage and serious mental and psychiatric illnesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Research from the United Nations (UN) Office on Drugs and Crime has shown that in places where cannabis has been legalised, the proportion of people with (a) psychiatric disorders and (b) suicides associated with regular cannabis use has increased, together with the number of hospitalisations.

sections.label: Body Worn Camera for officers
sections.summary: The Body Worn Camera has made a meaningful difference to officers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Body Worn Camera (BWC) has made a meaningful difference to our officers.

sections.label: PolCam effectiveness solving crime
sections.summary: PolCam is effective in deterring, detecting and solving crime, helping Police solve around 7,500 cases.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: PolCam has proven to be very effective in deterring, detecting and solving crime.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They have helped Police to solve around 7,500 crime cases.

sections.label: PolCam deployment by mid-2030s
sections.summary: By the mid-2030s, SPF and HTX plan to deploy over 200,000 PolCams, more than double today's number.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: By the mid-2030s, SPF and the HTX plan to deploy a total of over 200,000 PolCams, more than double what we have today.

sections.label: Airport automated immigration lanes
sections.summary: By mid-year, 95% of arriving airport travellers would clear immigration via automated lanes, up from just over one-third pre-COVID.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: By the middle of the year, 95% of arriving travellers at the airport would be able to clear immigration using automated lanes, compared to just over one-third pre-COVID.

sections.label: Prison Automated Screening System development
sections.summary: SPS worked with HTX to develop the Prison Automated Screening System (PASS) to alleviate the tedium and unpleasantness of the task.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To alleviate the tedium and unpleasantness of this task, SPS has worked with HTX to develop the Prison Automated Screening System (PASS).

sections.label: AIM system rollout by 2026
sections.summary: Prisons and HTX intend to roll out the AIM system by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Prisons and HTX intend to roll out the AIM system by 2026.

sections.label: myResponder 2.0 app rollout
sections.summary: SCDF's myResponder 2.0 app will be rolled out later this year with new features including a video call function.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Another example is SCDF's myResponder 2.0 app that will be rolled out later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The app has new features, such as a video call function, which enables SCDF's Operations Centre to initiate live video streaming through the Community First Responders' mobile phone.

sections.label: Two-year recidivism rate halved
sections.summary: The two-year recidivism rate was halved between the 2000s and 2020s, from 40% to around 20% today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In this regard, our rehabilitation approach has been effective.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have halved the two-year recidivism rate between the 2000s and 2020s – from 40% then to around 20% today.

sections.label: Desistor Network launched last year
sections.summary: Last year Prisons launched the Desistor Network to strengthen supporting social agencies and create opportunities for desistors to support each other.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Ex-offenders need encouragement to forge pro-social networks and make lifestyle changes to stay on the straight and narrow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Hence, last year, Prisons launched the Desistor Network to strengthen the community of social agencies that support desistors and to create opportunities for desistors to support each other.

sections.label: Corrections 2030 transformation initiative
sections.summary: Prisons will embark on another major transformation initiative this year called Corrections 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Building on existing efforts, I am pleased to announce that Prisons will embark on another major transformation initiative this year – Corrections 2030.

sections.label: Family referrals and marriage support
sections.summary: Prisons has referred over 900 families for assistance, and from April 2024 inmates and families needing marriage support will be referred to Fam@FSC for counselling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To date, Prisons has referred more than 900 families for assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: From April 2024, inmates and their families who require marriage support, will also be referred to Strengthening Families Programme@Family Service Centre (Fam@FSC) for counselling.

sections.label: Five-year recidivism rate lowest
sections.summary: The five-year recidivism rate is at its lowest ever, 36.8% for the 2018 release cohort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The five-year recidivism rate is currently at its lowest ever – 36.8% for the 2018 release cohort.

sections.label: Revised training development framework
sections.summary: Prisons will make volunteer and community partner training more effective through a revised Development Framework for Offender Rehabilitation Personnel.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Prisons has been providing basic corrections-related training for volunteers and community partners who work with inmates, ex-offenders and their families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I am glad to announce that Prisons will make such training more effective through a revised Development Framework for Offender Rehabilitation Personnel.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim Organisations rehabilitation role
sections.summary: MMOs are key partners in culturally-nuanced rehabilitative programmes and helped reduce Malay/Muslim two-year recidivism from about 34% to 26% over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I will now speak in Malay on the role of Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs) in our rehabilitation efforts. :   Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs) are an important part of the ecosystem of support for Malay/Muslim inmates and ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: They are our key partners in developing culturally-nuanced rehabilitative programmes and have played a major role in reducing the two-year recidivism rate for Malay/Muslim offenders, from about 34% to 26% in the past decade.

sections.label: Supervision 2.0 and hair testing
sections.summary: CNB will enhance its approach under Supervision 2.0, generally replacing urine testing with hair testing as the default drug detection method during supervision.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To better curb long-term relapse, CNB will enhance its approach under a new "Supervision 2.0" regime. "Supervision 2.0" aims to better support supervisees' reintegration journey through more efficient monitoring.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: A key move is CNB's plans to generally replace urine testing with hair testing as the default drug detection method during supervision.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As hair retains evidence of drug consumption longer than urine, with similar testing reliability, hair testing will allow supervisees to report only once every quarter.

sections.label: CNB drug syndicates seized
sections.summary: CNB dismantled 25 drug syndicates at home and seized over $15 million worth of drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: At home, CNB dismantled 25 drug syndicates and seized more than $15 million worth of drugs.

sections.label: Scam cases and losses
sections.summary: Scam cases rose nearly 50% in 2023, with social engineering and deception scams causing 92% of about $650 million in losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The number of scam cases increased by close to 50% in 2023 while amounts lost to scams remained more or less the same since 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The increase in scam numbers was largely driven by scams using social engineering and deception to manipulate victims into transferring monies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: These scams accounted for 92% of scam losses, or about $600 million, out of approximately $650 million lost to scams in 2023.

sections.label: Scam victims under 50
sections.summary: Singaporeans under 50 made up 73% of total scam victims in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In fact, Singaporeans under 50 years old made up 73% of the total number of scam victims in 2023.

sections.label: Malware scams drop, SIM offences
sections.summary: Malware-enabled scams dropped 70% in the last quarter to about 280 cases, and offences will be introduced for misusing local SIM cards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: With this coordinated effort, we arrested the spike and, by the end of last year, the number of malware-enabled scams dropped 70% in the last quarter from the quarter before to about 280 cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To address this, we will introduce offences to deter the misuse of local SIM cards for scams and other criminal activities.

sections.label: Meta platforms exploited by scammers
sections.summary: Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram accounted for close to half of 2023 scam cases and about 43%, around $280 million, of losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Meta products, in particular, Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram, were among the top online platforms exploited by scammers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: They accounted for close to half of the scam cases in 2023, and about 43% – around $280 million – of losses.

sections.label: Shopee e-commerce scam drop
sections.summary: Shopee observed a 71% drop in e-commerce scams reported on its platform between 2021 and 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Shopee observed a sharp drop of 71% in e-commerce scams between 2021 and 2023 reported on their platform.

sections.label: Online Criminal Harms Act powers
sections.summary: The Online Criminal Harms Act will give Police legal powers to issue directions to online platforms to prevent scam accounts and content from reaching Singapore users.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The coming into force of the Online Criminal Harms Act, or OCHA, will give Police the legal powers to issue directions to online platforms to prevent scam accounts and content from interacting with or reaching Singapore users.

sections.label: Security officer wage increases
sections.summary: Entry-level outsourced security officer monthly gross wage rose to $2,650 from 1 January 2024 and will reach $3,530 by 2028, benefiting over 40,000 resident officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The monthly gross wage of an entry-level, full-time outsourced security officer was increased to $2,650 since 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: It will be raised to $3,530 by 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: More than 40,000 resident security officers will benefit from the PWM wage increases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: On shift hours raised by Ms Sylvia Lim, the new PWM wage schedule has already taken the first step to impose a maximum cap of 72 additional working hours per month.

sections.label: Figure fell from 180 to 63
sections.summary: In 2018 the figure was 180 and it went down to 63 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In 2018, it was 180 and it went down to 63 in 2022.

sections.label: No other designated PSPs
sections.summary: The Minister confirms there are no other individuals designated as PSPs beyond those publicly announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: If not, is the Minister able to share if there are other individuals designated as PSPs, that have not been publicly announced?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I can confirm that there are no other designated PSPs in the sense that the Member is asking.

sections.label: Home Team volunteer numbers rise
sections.summary: Total COPs, VSCs and CDAU volunteers rose from 5,202 in 2019 to 7,105 last year, and recruitment efforts are being increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Total number of COPs, VSCs and CDAU volunteers – between 2019 and 2023; if you take the total number of volunteers – 5,202 in 2019, last year was 7,105.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, overall, the total number of Home Team volunteers has increased over the five years and we are trying to increase our recruitment efforts.

sections.label: Withdrawal of COS amendment
sections.summary: The speaker thanks Members for 32 cuts in the COS debate, says the Home Team and MHA officers do their duty well, and withdraws his amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I would like to express my appreciation to the hon Members for making 32 cuts and providing very thoughtful points in this COS debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: But we are all united on one thing: that the Home Team officers and the MHA officers are doing a good job in keeping our country safe and secure, and this duty is done without fear of favour and with integrity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: It also reflects the trust and confidence that our members of the public have in the Home Team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: With that, Sir, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
